- Windows 7 desktop: the real Start orb in its three states (normal, lit while the Start menu is open, pressed while it is held, faded between them); the supplied Windows 7 Control Panel icon; a notification area with the arrow that opens the hidden icons (firewall, Action Center, update, Bluetooth, removable storage, MSN), the Action Center flag, the network and the volume, and MSN (Messages) keeps a small icon there once it was opened, as if it ran in the background.
- Desktop: the "Customize the menu" rows are only in the launcher settings now (Context menu); the menu of a file or folder has Cut and Copy (and Paste on a folder), and the desktop's own menu has Paste (into a Desktop folder, each file also put on the desktop), all arranged in the same Context menu settings. The icon grid has a new switch, "Fill empty spaces", off by default: an icon moved away leaves its hole, the others keep their places and a new icon goes after the last one. A bug is fixed: an icon that had been moved started its next drag from its old place instead of from where it is.
- Windows 11 launcher: its own accent colour (Launcher settings; the look's own blue until one is picked) for the Start logo, the bars under open windows, the clock flyout and the selections.
- Music player (Windows Media Player 12 look): the forward key was squeezed out of the pill and showed as a dot; the times moved above the pill and the volume shows only when there is room. A Lyrics button shows the song's lyrics in the middle in place of the cover.
- Music search: play and shuffle for everything found (lyrics hits excluded), the songs, albums and artists each with their own play and shuffle, albums with their cover and artists with their picture, a small play button on a lyrics hit that is a song of the phone, and the lyrics last. Artist and album pages have a search box, a cover with soft corners, and round play and shuffle buttons floating over the cover instead of between it and the black. An artist page shows the artist's own picture, fetched by name (Deezer's public search, only with Settings > online covers on, kept on the phone), not an album cover.
- Music player, Blended cover: the cover and its own mirror image are blurred together as one picture, so the bottom of the cover goes on seamlessly (before it faded into a differently cropped, darker copy), the darkening comes only towards the foot, and the whole backdrop now slides with the cover when you swipe to the previous or next song (before it stayed still while the cover was swiped).
- Weather: the moon is drawn with its real seas (Procellarum, Imbrium, Serenitatis, Tranquillitatis, Crisium, Nubium, Humorum), Tycho with its rays, Copernicus and rimmed craters, in the scene icons and in the phase card, with the face the right way round for a waning moon too.
- Task Manager: the column Processes is sorted by (CPU, memory ...) and the graph chosen in Performance are remembered.
- Game Hub: the shelf shows every game of the Mega Games page (126 in all, it showed only the first fifty); a game without a picture of its own gets a made cover (its colour from its name, its mark, group and name). The game page is laid out like the store pages: the cover blurred behind the head, the case with a shadow, round Open and More buttons, underlined Overview and Settings tabs, and the game's own text on Overview (Steam, Wikipedia or the Play Store, fetched once and kept) instead of "Opens the game". A hidden game wears a small eye mark on its case and its page says "Hidden on the phone" (hidden means hidden from the phone's home screen and app list, not from the shelf). The in-game menu handle is a thin line on the screen's edge, on by default, and it fades out after 10 seconds untouched (a touch brings it back, a second one opens the menu).
